notes: BALANCE replaced with 'scale'. The page glosses it balanza, but 'balance' does not mean a
weighing instrument in current English — the same class of error as 'clime' on page 10.
'pipe' dropped: on a tools page it reads as plumbing, but the gloss is pipa, the smoking
kind. Ambiguous either way and not really a tool.
Collisions kept together: wrench/spanner (spanner is British), lantern/flashlight
'seal' here is the stamp; the animal is in another area. 'clip' also appears as paper clip
in Food and Ingredients, and 'washer' is the metal ring, unrelated to the machine in The
EASY: workshop vocabulary asks more of a learner than naming what is in a room.

area.name: Tools
area.description: Las herramientas de una caja y de un taller: para atornillar, cortar, medir, alumbrar y sujetar.

units.name: Hand tools
units.topic: The tools that turn and grip. 'wrench' and 'spanner' are the same tool — wrench is American, spanner British — and a monkey wrench adjusts to fit

units.name: Cutting and drilling
units.topic: The tools that make a hole or take material away. A bit is the part of a drill that turns, a handsaw is a saw used by hand

units.name: Screws and nails
units.topic: The small metal pieces that hold things together. A washer is the flat ring that sits under a nut

units.name: Keys, locks and switches
units.topic: What opens, closes and hangs. 'hook' and 'hanger' are both gancho — a hanger holds clothes, a hook holds anything

units.name: Garden and building
units.topic: The larger tools used outdoors and on a building site

units.name: Sticking and measuring
units.topic: What joins things and what measures them. 'tape' and 'ribbon' are both cinta — tape sticks, ribbon decorates. 'seal' here is the stamp pressed into a document

units.name: Light and fire
units.topic: What gives light when there is none, and what you lean on. 'lantern' and 'flashlight' are both linterna — a flashlight is the handheld electric one. 'cane' and 'stick' are both bastón
